newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar/yen turnover in Tokyo hits 6-year high.
newsitem.headline: Dollar/yen turnover in Tokyo hits 6-year high.

text.p: The volume of dollars traded for yen in Tokyo in 1996 was at a six-year high as of the end of November, figures compiled by the Foreign Exchange and Money Brokers Association showed on Friday.
The total turnover of dollars for yen in spot and swap transactions was around $5.2 trillion as of end-November, the figures showed. Turnover for the whole of 1995 was around $5.1 trillion.
Record-low domestic interest rates and a relatively stable exchange rate lured Japanese operators into heavy investment in high-yielding overseas securities this year, dealers said.
This necessitated sales of yen for dollars and other currencies, keeping volume brisk for much of the year.

Particularly notable was strong investment in Australian dollars due to the steady issue of dual-currency samurai bonds, which helped push that currency to a four-year high against the yen in November. Sterling and the mark also made phenomenal gains.
The all-time peak for turnover in Tokyo is $5.96 trillion in 1990. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk + 81-3-3432-8806
